national.line: A strawberry farmer's cell number ended up in an English exam question, and now he uses the calls he gets to inspire students; one caller has been accepted into a prestigious university. Wrong number, right outcome.
A violin teacher of 40 years, known as the Godmother of Korean Violin, got a surprise goodbye performance from 100 violins and one unforgettable song. Not a dry eye in the room.
An Idaho man who holds the most concurrent Guinness World Records moved more than 2 pounds of ice cubes between two trays using only his mouth. Brain freeze not included.
Guatemalan chefs in the capital prepared a record-breaking fiambre salad that weighed 4,325.9 pounds. Pass the fork.
Thousands of concertgoers in Poland spontaneously sang 'Bohemian Rhapsody,' and it sounded flawless. Nobody argued over who sings the high part.
A rescued bear in Bosnia now weighs 330 pounds and still tries to sit in her rescuer's lap. She never got the memo about her size.
The Minnesota Zoo welcomed three orphaned brown bear cubs rescued from Alaska. The cutest new neighbors in the state.

pride.line: Eight people received the Lebanon Fire Department's Life Saving Award on Oct. 26 for saving a Missouri Cooperage worker who collapsed July 8: coworker Tyler Blattel, Lt. Joe Gerber, Capt. Terry Saltzman, firefighters Adam Moppin, Nick Davis and Paul Shomo, Mercy EMS paramedic Louis Corbeil and EMT Jeremy Vinson. Now that's a team effort.
pride.label: Life Saving Award

pride.line: Ollie Sanders, a Lebanon High School color guard member whose favorite moment was winning best colorguard at Carthage, is the Yellowjacket of the Week. Spin on, Ollie.
pride.label: Yellowjacket of the Week

pride.line: Lebanon Schools named Katie Cottongim its new Director of Communications this week. Now the snow day news has a home.
pride.label: New Director

pride.line: Bolivar High School senior Chapel Banner earned a four-year Navy ROTC scholarship covering full tuition, one of about 100 students picked nationwide this year. That's some serious college money.
pride.label: Scholarship

pride.line: Julia Jones, a Bolivar High School graduate, finished her Dental Assistant apprenticeship through OCHC's Bolivar clinic and the BoMo Works program, and plans to become a dental hygienist. She has plenty to smile about.
pride.label: Apprenticeship

pride.line: Bolivar softball beat Aurora 12-2 for the district title, then reached the state quarterfinal, where it fell 16-5 to Southern Boone on Oct. 24. Plenty to cheer about.
pride.label: District Champions

pride.line: Victoria Moroski, 17, of the Lake of the Ozarks won gold in the under-18 women's skim division at the World Wakesurf Championships in Hangzhou, China, in October, and Team USA won gold too. Smooth sailing, or surfing.
pride.label: World Champion

pride.line: Waynesville Career Center welding students, led by instructor Adam Rodden, built backdrop props for band director Jared Sabatasso's Tiger Pride Marching Band and saved the band about $10,000. A welding job well done.
pride.label: Students Save Band $10,000

local.line: Level Up Lebanon wrapped its biggest season yet, with Ward 1 and Ward 4 residents hauling roughly 200 cars' worth of cleanup this fall. That's a lot of trunk space.
The Osage Beach Chick-fil-A opens Thursday, Nov. 5. Lake traffic is about to get tastier.
Camdenton R-III broke ground on its new Early Childhood Center on Tuesday, Oct. 27, with preschoolers on hand. The tiniest crew did the cutest work.

Camden County Public Water Supply District No. 5 got a $223,000 interest-free loan from the Missouri Department of Natural Resources to plan and design drinking water upgrades. Interest-free is the best kind of free.
Lake Regional Clinic in Osage Beach welcomed pediatric nurse practitioner Courtney Wood, who offers walk-in acute care, well-child visits and sports physicals. Good news for scraped knees.

music.line: CMA CEO Sarah Trahern says the 60th CMA Awards will spotlight the '90s country stars who still influence today's artists, with Lainey Wilson hosting. Cue the cowboy hats and big hair.
Hudson Westbrook revealed the tracklist for his new album 'Made You Look.' Time to start picking favorites.
Ella Langley closes her Dandelion Tour in Saint Paul on Oct. 31. What a way to end a tour.
Luke Bryan cut Zach King from 'American Idol,' and years later King is touring with him. Turns out the cut was just the opening act.
Jon Pardi, Zach Top, Thomas Rhett and Hudson Westbrook will perform at the 2027 Country Thunder Wisconsin Festival. Wisconsin is about to get twangy.
The Under The Big Sky Fest revealed its 2027 lineup, led by Zach Bryan and Kacey Musgraves. Start saving now.
Country star Pat Green will release a live album recorded in an iconic Texas hall. Boots and bleachers, all in one record.
Canadian singer Jess Moskaluke will make her Grand Ole Opry debut as part of the Canadian Country Music Association's 50th birthday celebration. Canada's sending its best to Nashville.

weird.line: An Ohio mail carrier who had never grown a regular pumpkin broke the state record with a 2,513-pound pumpkin from his backyard and won $9,250. Talk about special delivery.

Raising Cane's founder Todd Graves turned a 3,156-pound pumpkin grown by Ron Wallace into the world's heaviest jack-o'-lantern in Salem on Oct. 27, beating the old mark by 407 pounds. Somebody had a lot of seeds to scoop.
An Aberdeen teen grew an 860-pound pumpkin on her grandfather's farm. That's one big pie.
3,400 drones lit up the night sky to form a giant peacock and set a world record. Not one feather fell.
A daredevil collector set a Guinness World Record by ripping open trading cards while strapped to the wing of a flying plane. Hope he got the rare one.
A woman reeled in a record-breaking sturgeon weighing over 1,000 pounds in the Fraser Valley. Bigger than most boats' coolers.
The world's largest pop-up book debuted in Los Angeles. Some story, standing up.
A 6-year-old flipped over a rock hoping for a common fossil and found a rare creature from a long-vanished ancient sea. Best show-and-tell ever.
A school tidy-up found a forgotten time capsule in the photocopy room. Somebody's old homework just got famous.
Austin firefighters say a raccoon stuck in a tree is alive and unharmed. Even the raccoon is relieved.
A couple spotted a raccoon stuck in a dumpster, and they helped in the cutest way possible. Trash panda, saved.
A bear with its head stuck in a bucket freed itself by ramming a rescue truck. Sometimes you just need a good bump.
A San Francisco tech startup is offering $20 an hour for dog walkers to spend four to six hours walking robot dogs. No treats required.
Tesla's Robotaxi wants 40 minutes to drive two blocks, and riders are baffled. Walking would have been faster.
Divers rescued a kangaroo that found itself over a mile from dry land. That's one long hop.
A Martian meteorite found in the Sahara is 4.1 billion years old. The oldest rock in the neighborhood.
After 35 years, Pennsylvania has a new record channel catfish. The old one finally got dethroned.
A Montana dinosaur fossil nicknamed Jodi is now the second most expensive fossil on auction records. Priciest bones in the barn.
Pumpkins were bred by ancient megafauna like mastodons to spread seeds, and they should have gone extinct thousands of years ago. They survived on pie power.
PBS Eons explored how pumpkins nearly went extinct with the mastodons until humans domesticated them. Thank you, pie.
A bear in Alaska spotted with multiple tapeworms earned an unusual 'Host with the Most' award. Not the trophy anyone wants.

humor.line: The first doughnuts in America were little 'nuts' of dough that the Pilgrims brought to New England after learning to make them in Holland. That's the whole story, hole and all.
Lemurs call Madagascar home, an island nation about 250 miles off the east coast of Africa. That's a long way to go for a banana.
Fazoli's and Olive Garden both acknowledged the day by at least 2016, and Little Caesars offered a Crazy Bread promotion. Carb loading counts as a holiday.
Candy corn is shaped like a corn kernel, with a yellow end, orange middle and white tip, and it's made from sugar, corn syrup and confectioner's wax. Yes, you've been eating wax.
National Pumpkin Day was less than a week ago, so there's probably an extra pumpkin sitting around, ready to become bread. Leftover pumpkin finally has a job.
WICKED the Musical founded this one in 2023. Even the calendar is defying gravity.
Rebecca Morgan started giving books to trick-or-treaters in 1995 in San Jose, California, because she didn't like that candy was the main Halloween treat. Plot twist at the front door.
The word pumpkin comes from the Greek word pepon, which means large melon. A large melon with a face on it.
Knock-knock jokes are some of the first jokes kids hear and learn, and anyone can tell one. Who's there? Dad, with another one.
It's also called Houdini Day, and it has been observed since 1927. Now you see it, now it's a holiday.
It's a day for adults handing out candy to sneak some for themselves before the kids start knocking. Quality control, parents call it.
Caramel apples are also called taffy apples, and the day falls right after apple harvest, on Halloween. Dentists see it coming.
Author Nancy Christie came up with it so people use the hour gained when clocks fall back to relax instead of work. Doing nothing finally has a holiday.
Spice maker McCormick created it in 2019 to start what it calls Cinnamon Season, and cinnamon comes from tree bark. Yes, you eat bark on purpose.
In 1884, representatives from 25 nations met in Washington, D.C., to agree on a common zero of longitude and standard time for the whole world. Somehow they all agreed on where zero is.
Nellie Verne Burt McPherson, president of the Bement, Illinois, Women's Club, thought it up in 1928 to thank her favorite author, Irving Bacheller. Fan mail got a calendar date.
It's a day to stop thinking about everything you 'should' do, like exercising, eating healthier and getting organized. Permission to ignore the laundry.
Vinegar is used for pickling cucumbers, cleaning, gardening and pest control. The sour jack of all trades.
It encourages owners to cook a homemade meal for any pet, not only dogs and cats. Fido is getting the good china.
It falls on Cookie Monster's birthday, and he first appeared on Sesame Street in 1969 after getting his start in 1966. Naturally, the cake is gone.
It's geared toward young kids learning shapes, but anyone can look for and point out circles. Round and round we go.
Deviled eggs are also known as eggs mimosa, stuffed eggs and dressed eggs. So many names for one party tray.
It honors everyone in radio and TV traffic departments who schedule and work very diligently. Thanks for keeping us on schedule.
It falls on the birthday of John Montagu, the fourth Earl of Sandwich. Lunch has a noble history.
Jellyfish are about 95 percent water and are not actually fish. Basically a swimming water balloon.
It's a day to give a dollar to someone you know, because a dollar can still get you a few things. Cheapest good deed of the year.
People use overused phrases as much as possible, to the point of irritation. It's a no-brainer, at the end of the day.
British archaeologist Howard Carter found King Tut's tomb in the Valley of the Kings in 1922, after first arriving in Egypt in 1891. Worth the wait, King Tut.
Kenner introduced the Easy-Bake Oven in 1963, and the original used ordinary incandescent light bulbs as its heat source. Cooking by lamp, the original air fryer.

It celebrates Dr. Marthenia 'Tina' Dupree, 'The Chicken Lady,' who spent twelve years as Director of Community Relations at one of the largest chicken restaurants in the world. Now that's a flock of fans.
Today you can give in to your sweet tooth and eat as much candy as you want. Mom and Dad finally agree.
It started in response to big banks planning to charge fees many people saw as excessive, and it encourages moving money to not-for-profit credit unions. Fees were the villain of this story.
American football grew out of rugby football, and its rules changed a lot over time. Every fan still argues about the rules.
Most men cook, but some feel lost in kitchens, and this day is for those men to attempt dinner. Smoke detector, standing by.
Stephanie and Adrienne Vendetti created it to empower redheaded women to love their hair and remind women of every hair color to love who they are. Redheads, take a bow.
